articles.title_en: The Emerging Role of Competition in Health Care
articles.title_cn: 竞争在医疗保健中的新兴作用
articles.abstract_en: This essay, commissioned to serve as an introduction to the JEP symposium on current competition in health care, provides a historical perspective on the role of both competition and regulation in the financing and delivery of health services since the implementation of Medicare and Medicaid in the mid-1960s. At the beginning of this period, few could perceive a role for competition in healthcare given the key role played by physicians in providing and ordering care and concerns that lower prices might signal lower quality. Initial attempts to slow rapidly rising costs involved various regulatory tools, but over time, regulation increasingly incorporated incentives for providers, to control costs. Competitive approaches began to develop in the late 1970s, in part reflecting broad changes in the nation’s political culture. Competitive approaches are now are quite widespread, but regulation plays an important role in the structuring of competition and in addressing areas where competition is seen as having less potential.
articles.abstract_cn: 本文受委托为 JEP 研讨会介绍当前医疗保健领域的竞争，提供了自 1960 中期实施 Medicare 和 Medicaid 以来竞争和监管在医疗服务融资和提供中的作用的历史视角。在此时期初期，考虑到医生在提供和订购医疗服务方面发挥的关键作用，以及人们担心较低的价格可能意味着较低的质量，很少有人能够意识到医疗保健领域竞争的作用。最初试图减缓成本快速上升的速度涉及各种监管工具，但随着时间的推移，监管越来越多地纳入对提供商的激励措施，以控制成本。竞争性方法在 1970 后期开始发展，部分反映了国家政治文化的广泛变化。竞争方法现在相当普遍，但监管在竞争结构和解决竞争被认为潜力较小的领域方面发挥着重要作用。

articles.abstract_en: The United States relies primarily on private health insurance markets, yet these markets are highly concentrated and becoming more so over time. We document concentration across commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid markets. We then examine how asymmetric information—particularly adverse selection—interacts with market power to shape premiums, plan design, and consumer welfare. Empirical evidence confirms that insurer consolidation raises premiums. We discuss how antitrust enforcement, risk adjustment, regulation, and informational interventions shape competition and consumer welfare in these markets.
articles.abstract_cn: 美国主要依赖私人健康保险市场，但这些市场高度集中，并且随着时间的推移变得更加集中。我们记录了商业、医疗保险优势和医疗补助市场的集中度。然后，我们研究不对称信息（尤其是逆向选择）如何与市场力量相互作用，从而影响保费、计划设计和消费者福利。经验证据证实保险公司合并会提高保费。我们讨论反垄断执法、风险调整、监管和信息干预如何影响这些市场的竞争和消费者福利。

articles.title_en: Regulated Competition in Health Insurance Markets on Two Sides of the Atlantic
articles.title_cn: 二 大西洋两岸健康保险市场的监管竞争
articles.abstract_en: Many high-income countries implement their policy of universal health insurance by individual health insurance in combination with regulated competition among insurers. Supported by public intervention, regulated competition can, in principle, address market failures in health insurance and smooth out some inequities in the financial consequences of ill health and in the ability to pay for health insurance. We compare the national systems in Germany, the Netherlands, and Switzerland to the US Marketplaces, all of which use versions of regulated competition. While they show many similarities (for example, open enrollment, community-rated premiums with subsidies, comprehensive benefit package, risk adjustment), we focus on three major differences and their implications for market functioning: (1) mandatory and universal versus voluntary and partial (applying to only one sector of health insurance); (2) greater or lesser profit orientation of insurers; and (3) reliance on markets or regulation to contain costs.
articles.abstract_cn: 许多高收入国家通过个人健康保险结合保险公司之间的规范竞争来实施全民健康保险政策。在公共干预的支持下，受监管的竞争原则上可以解决健康保险市场失灵的问题，并消除健康不良造成的财务后果和健康保险支付能力方面的一些不平等现象。我们将德国、荷兰和瑞士的国家系统与美国市场进行比较，所有这些国家都使用受监管竞争的版本。虽然它们表现出许多相似之处（例如，开放注册、社区定额保费和补贴、综合福利方案、风险调整），但我们重点关注 三 的主要差异及其对市场运作的影响：（1）强制性和普遍性与自愿性和部分性（仅适用于健康保险的 一 部门）； (2) 保险公司的利润导向或多或少； (3) 依靠市场或监管来控制成本。

articles.title_en: Anticompetitive Contracts Between Insurers and Providers in Health Care
articles.title_cn: 保险公司与医疗保健提供者之间的反竞争合同
articles.abstract_en: For people with private health insurance in the United States, contracts between insurers and providers are important to fostering health care competition and improving efficiency. However, insurer-provider contract provisions do not always advance competition and consumer welfare. This essay discusses the contracting strategies used by insurers to increase competition, and four anticompetitive contract terms: anti-tiering or anti-steering, all-or-nothing, most favored nation, and gag clauses, that may be used by dominant health systems to protect themselves from competition. I conclude with a discussion of policy responses that can be used to address provider use of anticompetitive clauses and that can reduce the negative impacts of provider market power. Understanding anticompetitive contract provisions and the potential policy responses to limit their impact is critical to health care competition.
articles.abstract_cn: 对于在美国拥有私人医疗保险的人来说，保险公司和提供者之间的合同对于促进医疗保健竞争和提高效率非常重要。然而，保险公司-提供商合同条款并不总是能促进竞争和消费者福利。本文讨论了保险公司为增加竞争而使用的签约策略，以及 四 反竞争合同条款：反分级或反转向、全有或全无、最惠国待遇和禁止性条款，这些条款可能被占主导地位的卫生系统用来保护自己免受竞争。最后，我讨论了可用于解决供应商使用反竞争条款并减少供应商市场力量的负面影响的政策反应。了解反竞争合同条款以及限制其影响的潜在政策应对措施对于医疗保健竞争至关重要。

articles.title_en: The Current Era of Health Care Consolidation
articles.title_cn: 当前医疗保健整合时代
articles.abstract_en: Consolidation in the last few decades has reshaped the organization and structure of US health care markets, among both providers and insurers. Nearly all US hospital and insurer markets exceed established regulatory thresholds for competitive markets, and over half of physicians are now employed by a hospital or health system, which can increase spending for patients, payers, and taxpayers. Increased supply-side concentration can alter the balance of negotiations between providers and insurers. Prices for patients with commercial insurance are approximately 2.5 times the prices paid by those with public insurance. High and variable prices have minimal link with higher quality, and the United States leads peer nations in health care spending. These dynamics have created ongoing national debates over an “affordability crisis” and generates frustrations with the US health care system. This article discusses sources of rising health care spending and potential policy solutions.
articles.abstract_cn: 过去几十年的整合重塑了美国医疗保健市场的组织和结构，包括供应商和保险公司。几乎所有美国医院和保险公司市场都超过了竞争市场的既定监管门槛，超过一半的医生现在受雇于医院或卫生系统，这可能会增加患者、付款人和纳税人的支出。供应方集中度的提高可能会改变提供商和保险公司之间的谈判平衡。拥有商业保险的患者的价格大约是拥有公共保险的患者支付的价格的 2.5 倍。高且不稳定的价格与更高的质量之间的联系微乎其微，而美国在医疗保健支出方面领先于其他国家。这些动态引发了关于“负担能力危机”的持续全国性辩论，并引发了人们对美国医疗保健系统的不满。本文讨论医疗保健支出增加的来源和潜在的政策解决方案。

articles.abstract_en: We describe competition in the physician market, focusing on how entry barriers and substitution possibilities have changed in recent decades. Regulatory caps on medical school seats and residency slots—especially for high-paying specialties—continue to ration entry, generate high returns for those who gain these slots, and direct the most academically accomplished trainees toward lucrative fields. But trained physicians increasingly compete with nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and other mid-level practitioners in the market for patients. Training of these substitutes has expanded far more rapidly than physician supply. We present key facts about the physician pipeline, a conceptual framework linking specialty earnings to entry barriers, and describe the rise of mid-level providers. These facts mean that effective competition policy in physician markets must look beyond conventional concentration measures and focus on the institutions and laws that govern who can provide medical care.
articles.abstract_cn: 我们描述了医生市场的竞争，重点关注近几十年来进入壁垒和替代可能性的变化。对医学院席位和住院医师名额的监管上限（特别是针对高薪专业）继续限制入学，为获得这些名额的人带来高回报，并将学术上最有成就的学员引向利润丰厚的领域。但训练有素的医生越来越多地与执业护士、医师助理和其他中级执业人员在患者市场上竞争。这些替代人员的培训扩张速度远远快于医生供应的扩张速度。我们介绍了有关医生管道的关键事实，一个将专业收入与进入壁垒联系起来的概念框架，并描述了中级医疗服务提供者的崛起。这些事实意味着，医生市场中有效的竞争政策必须超越传统的集中措施，重点关注管理谁可以提供医疗服务的机构和法律。

articles.title_en: Substitutes for Success? Public Versus Private Competition in Medicare Advantage
articles.title_cn: 成功的替代品？医疗保险优势方面的公共与私人竞争
articles.abstract_en: We assess the evolving role of competition in Medicare Advantage and its implications for beneficiary welfare. We describe how competition from the public option, traditional Medicare, and other private insurers within Medicare Advantage act as substitutes in incentivizing plans to deliver value. We show that while historically the choice between traditional Medicare and Medicare Advantage provided a vital competitive dynamic, traditional Medicare's strength as a competitor has declined significantly, driven by generous payments favoring private plans. Consequently, the burden of ensuring value for enrollees has shifted to competition within the Medicare Advantage market. While county-level competition among private insurers has increased, this growth is primarily driven by the expansion of large national carriers rather than new entrants. Insurers still wield substantial market power due to significant barriers to entry, raising concerns about the ability of the program to incentivize private insurers to use public dollars to maximize value for beneficiaries.
articles.abstract_cn: 我们评估了竞争在 Medicare Advantage 中不断变化的作用及其对受益人福利的影响。我们描述了来自公共选择、传统医疗保险和医疗保险优势内其他私人保险公司的竞争如何作为激励计划提供价值的替代品。我们表明，虽然从历史上看，传统医疗保险和医疗保险优势之间的选择提供了至关重要的竞争动力，但由于有利于私人计划的慷慨支付，传统医疗保险作为竞争对手的实力已显着下降。因此，确保参保者价值的负担已转移到 Medicare Advantage 市场内的竞争上。虽然县级私营保险公司之间的竞争有所加剧，但这种增长主要是由大型全国性保险公司的扩张而非新进入者推动的。由于存在巨大的进入壁垒，保险公司仍然拥有巨大的市场力量，这引发了人们对该计划能否激励私人保险公司使用公共资金为受益人实现价值最大化的担忧。

articles.title_en: Understanding Medicaid Managed Care: The Procured Competition Model
articles.title_cn: 了解医疗补助管理式医疗：采购竞争模式
articles.abstract_en: Medicaid is one of the largest public programs in the United States—providing health insurance to over 75 million low-income Americans—and over three quarters of its enrollees receive care via private “managed care” insurers. In this article, we make three central points about the economics of contracting out Medicaid to private insurers. First, the empirical evidence on Medicaid privatization is mixed: contracting out has not meaningfully reduced public costs or improved quality of care. Second, we propose a framework, which we call “procured competition,” to describe the unique structure of Medicaid managed care as a hybrid of public procurement and regulated competition. Third, we discuss the key policy levers across procurement, competition, and consumer choice in this model. Throughout, we highlight open research questions, arguing that the enormous variation in how states design these programs—combined with limited evidence on what works—represents a promising area for high-impact scholarship.
articles.abstract_cn: 医疗补助计划是美国最大的公共计划之一，为超过 75 百万 名低收入美国人提供健康保险，超过 三 四分之一的参保者通过私人“管理式医疗”保险公司获得医疗服务。在本文中，我们以 三 为中心，阐述将医疗补助计划外包给私人保险公司的经济效益。 第一，医疗补助私有化的经验证据好坏参半：外包并没有显着降低公共成本或提高护理质量。 第二，我们提出了一个框架，我们称之为“采购竞争”，来描述医疗补助管理式医疗的独特结构，作为公共采购和监管竞争的混合体。 第三，我们讨论了该模型中采购、竞争和消费者选择的关键政策杠杆。自始至终，我们都强调开放性研究问题，认为各州设计这些项目的方式存在巨大差异，再加上有效的证据有限，代表了高影响力学术的一个有前途的领域。

articles.title_en: A Users’ Guide to Uncovering Worker and Firm Effects: The ABC of AKM
articles.title_cn: 揭示工人和公司影响的用户指南：AKM ABC
articles.abstract_en: The AKM model introduced by Abowd, Kramarz, and Margolis (1999) has become a workhorse to study worker and firm heterogeneity, and to understand the sources of wage dispersion in the labor market using linked employer-employee data. In this article, we introduce the model and estimator, discuss some best practices for estimation, and review some empirical findings on the role of worker and firm heterogeneity in wage dispersion. While the AKM methodology has proven useful to analyze a host of questions in a variety of settings within labor economics and beyond, we also point to the need for methodological developments.
articles.abstract_cn: Abowd、Kramarz 和 Margolis (1999) 提出的 AKM 模型已成为研究工人和企业异质性的主力，并使用关联的雇主-雇员数据了解劳动力市场工资离散的来源。在本文中，我们介绍了模型和估计器，讨论了一些估计的最佳实践，并回顾了有关工人和企业异质性在工资分散中的作用的一些实证研究结果。虽然 AKM 方法已被证明有助于分析劳动经济学及其他领域的各种环境中的许多问题，但我们也指出了方法论发展的必要性。

articles.title_en: The Economics of Paid Sick Leave
articles.abstract_en: This article examines the economics of paid sick leave from both theoretical and empirical perspectives. Research on paid sick leave has evolved dynamically over the last decade, primarily driven by the spread of US sick pay mandates, which have increased paid sick leave access from 63 percent to 77 percent in all US jobs. We begin by discussing the economic rationales for government regulation of paid sick leave, particularly the negative externalities associated with contagious diseases when individuals work while sick. After that, we discuss the key trade-offs in the general design of paid sick leave schemes, along with the trade-offs when setting specific policy parameters. Finally, we review economic modeling approaches to study optimal paid sick leave policies.
articles.abstract_cn: 本文从理论和实证角度探讨了带薪病假的经济学。过去十年中，带薪病假研究不断发展，这主要是受美国病假工资强制规定的推动，这使得美国所有工作中带薪病假的使用范围从 63% 增加到 77%。我们首先讨论政府监管带薪病假的经济原理，特别是当个人带病工作时与传染病相关的负外部性。之后，我们讨论带薪病假计划总体设计中的关键权衡，以及设定具体政策参数时的权衡。最后，我们回顾了研究最佳带薪病假政策的经济模型方法。

articles.abstract_en: The dollar shortage debate—Paul Samuelson called it “the big open question of our time”—dominated international macroeconomics in the 15 years following the end of World War II. There were two main views regarding its cause: financial frictions that limited capital flows to Western Europe (Kindleberger); and overvalued fixed exchange rates versus the US dollar (Friedman). According to Kindleberger the dollar shortage was attenuated by two real factors that contributed to current account deficits: a large technological gap between the United States and Europe; and European impatience to improve living standards. Kindleberger believed that the current account deficit would prove chronic because of the persistence of the productivity gap, a view that was challenged by Bloomfield who argued that it would dissipate through income growth in Europe. We argue that Kindelberger’s analytical framework is closely connected to the modern intertemporal approach to current account determination; and, also, that the international reserve function of the US dollar—the Triffin dilemma—did not play a role in the dollar shortage.
articles.abstract_cn: 美元短缺的争论——保罗·萨缪尔森称之为“我们这个时代的重大悬而未决的问题”——在二战结束后的 15 年间主导了国际宏观经济。 二 对其原因有主要观点：金融摩擦限制了资本流向西欧（Kindleberger）；以及对美元的固定汇率被高估（弗里德曼）。根据金德尔伯格的说法，导致经常账户赤字的 二 真实因素削弱了美元短缺：美国和欧洲之间巨大的技术差距；以及欧洲对提高生活水平的不耐烦。金德尔伯格认为，由于生产率差距的持续存在，经常账户赤字将长期存在，这一观点受到布卢姆菲尔德的挑战，他认为经常账户赤字将通过欧洲收入增长而消失。我们认为，金德尔伯格的分析框架与经常账户确定的现代跨期方法密切相关。此外，美元的国际储备功能——特里芬困境——并没有在美元短缺中发挥作用。
